tasks.short: Respond on site to alarms and threats

steps.what: Show the alarm and the response procedure
Respond to intrusion alarms on site

tasks.design: The {OPS_SYSTEM} shows the alarm and the response procedure. Responding to medical emergencies, threats, fire, or intrusion stays on site. The manager logs what was done against the procedure.
tasks.previous_blocker: The procedure was a binder, and the alarm was a phone call.
tasks.enabler_now: An alarm row can show the type and the matching procedure.
tasks.still_hard: Going to the alarm cannot be done from a screen.
tasks.human_edge: The manager judges the scene, including a false alarm.
tasks.altitude: The response still happens on site. The procedure is on the alarm instead of in a binder.

reach.task: Meet the manager at the alarm

evidence.claim: Showing a stored procedure next to an alarm is configuration. The source pack says security work in this group is ticket and incident-log configuration, and that the judgement stays with a person.

assumptions: The work starts when an alarm is raised and ends when the on-site response is logged.
An alarm has an id, a type, a place, and a time, produced by the detector or the person who called. A type with no stored procedure is shown as missing and is not invented.
Time a system already spends running is not counted as the security manager's effort.
A draft that cites an identifier which is not in the store is discarded.
The incremental hours retire stale drafts when source rows change.
unknowns: Whether medical, fire, and intrusion alarms share one log.
research_questions: Which alarm types have a written procedure today?

already_counted.description: Time at the alarm is already in the response step.

incremental.description: Correct a log line if the alarm type was wrong.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Saving falls when the alarm is only a phone call. The response stays on site. The range is below that case.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Evaluate security operations from audit measures

steps.what: Pull security operations measures for auditing
Draft the assessment from those measures

loop.purpose: Draft an assessment that cites only measures from the audit period.
loop.output: An assessment whose every figure cites a stored measure.
loop.check: Every cited id exists in the period, and no risk is added.
loop.stop: Stop when the period has no measures.
loop.why_not_simpler: A fixed checklist cannot say which measures were missing.

steps.what: Evaluate security risks found in auditing

tasks.design: Operations measures for the period are pulled on {BI}. A draft assessment cites only those measures. The security manager evaluates the risks, and that evaluation is what gets filed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Audits were rebuilt from scattered logs each quarter.
tasks.enabler_now: Measures can be queried for a named period.
tasks.still_hard: Naming a risk, and whether it is worth acting on, stays a judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The manager knows which measure does not describe the real operation.

ambition.what: A closed period can be assessed in the same week, and a draft with no measures is not filed.

tasks.altitude: The week is the evaluation, not the hunt for last quarter's figures.

evidence.claim: The source pack says security work in this group is ticket and incident-log configuration, and that the judgement stays with a person. An assessment that cites stored measures can be checked. It does not decide the risk.

assumptions: The work starts when an audit period closes and ends when the manager's evaluation is filed.
A measure has an id, a period, and a value, produced by the operations log. A period with no rows is not assessed.
Time a system already spends running is not counted as the security manager's effort.
A draft that cites an identifier which is not in the store is discarded.
The incremental hours retire stale drafts when source rows change.
unknowns: Which operations measures are already stored by period.
research_questions: Who defines a reportable risk for this firm?

already_counted.description: Evaluating risks is already in the evaluation step.

incremental.description: Retire an assessment when a measure is corrected.

approvals.approved_version: evaluation the manager signed for that period

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Saving falls when the period has no stored measures. The evaluation stays. The range is below that case.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Issue security policies from stored standards

steps.what: Draft policies from those stored standards

loop.purpose: Draft policies that cite only stored security standards.
loop.input: Standard id and its current text.
loop.output: Draft policy clauses that each cite a standard id.
loop.check: Every clause cites a stored standard, and no new rule is added.
loop.stop: Stop when a standard id is missing or withdrawn.
loop.why_not_simpler: A template cannot show which standard a clause came from.

steps.what: Check procedures before they are used

tasks.design: Stored standards are gathered from {DOCS}. A draft policy cites only those standards. The security manager checks the procedures, and only that version is issued.
tasks.previous_blocker: Policies were copied forward and no longer matched the standard.
tasks.enabler_now: A standard can be stored with an id and a text.
tasks.still_hard: Whether a procedure is fit for this site stays a check by the manager.
tasks.human_edge: The manager knows which standard does not fit the building.

ambition.what: A changed standard can refresh the draft the same week, and the old text is not issued.

tasks.altitude: The week is the check, not the retyping of clauses that already exist.

evidence.claim: A policy draft that cites stored standards can be checked line by line. The source pack says security work in this group is ticket and incident-log configuration, and that the judgement stays with a person.

assumptions: The work starts when a standard is created or changed and ends when the manager issues the policies.
A standard has an id and text, produced by the last approved standard. A clause with no standard id is dropped.
Time a system already spends running is not counted as the security manager's effort.
A draft that cites an identifier which is not in the store is discarded.
The incremental hours retire stale drafts when source rows change.
unknowns: Whether standards already have stable identifiers.
research_questions: Who else must see a policy before it is issued?

already_counted.description: Checking procedures is already in the check step.

incremental.description: Retire an issued policy when its standard is withdrawn.

approvals.approved_version: procedures the manager checked against the current standards

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Saving falls when standards are not stored as clauses. The manager still checks before issue. The range is below that case.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Assess incident risks and file a response plan

steps.what: Draft a response plan from those incidents

loop.purpose: Draft a response plan that cites only recorded incidents.
loop.input: Incident id, consequence note, and date.
loop.output: Plan items that each cite an incident id.
loop.check: Every item cites a stored incident, and no consequence is invented.
loop.stop: Stop when the incident list is empty.
loop.why_not_simpler: A generic plan cannot show which incident it answers.

steps.what: Assess which risks the plan can mitigate

tasks.design: Recorded incidents and consequences are listed from the {OPS_SYSTEM}. A draft plan cites only those incidents. The security manager assesses which risks it can mitigate, and that version is filed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Response plans were rewritten without the incident list in front of the writer.
tasks.enabler_now: Incidents can be stored with a consequence note.
tasks.still_hard: Whether a plan actually mitigates a risk stays an assessment.
tasks.human_edge: The manager knows a consequence the note understates.
tasks.altitude: The plan starts from recorded incidents. The assessment of risk stays with the manager.

evidence.claim: The source pack says security work in this group is ticket and incident-log configuration, and that the judgement stays with a person. A plan that cites incident ids can be checked. It does not close the incident.

assumptions: The work starts when incidents with consequence notes exist and ends when the assessed response plan is filed.
An incident has an id, a date, and a consequence note, produced by the person who logged it. An incident with no note is listed and not given a consequence by the draft.
Time a system already spends running is not counted as the security manager's effort.
A draft that cites an identifier which is not in the store is discarded.
The incremental hours retire stale drafts when source rows change.
unknowns: Whether consequence notes are already on the incident row.
research_questions: Which risks this firm expects a response plan to cover?

already_counted.description: Assessing the plan is already in the assessment step.

incremental.description: Retire a plan item when its incident is corrected.

approvals.approved_version: plan the manager assessed for those incidents

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Saving falls when consequences are not on the incident. The assessment stays. The range is below that case.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Alarm response stays on site. An assessment cites measures that exist. Policies are issued only after the manager checks them. A response plan does not close an incident.
reach: The duty lead sees the procedure on the alarm.
An issued policy is the checked version.
skills_to_grow: Do not invent a procedure for an alarm type that has none.
Drop a policy clause that cites no standard.
role.ambitious_version: A changed standard refreshes the draft the same week, and the previous text is not what gets issued.
